propositions: A primary dedup guard (binding_store.is_comment_mapped) was silently inert in production for 6 days because the comment_ids map was never populated, surviving all review and test layers due to a working fallback (body-equality dedup) that masked the failure.

The primary dedup guard's inertness was never detected because it returns quietly on four conditions with no logging, metrics, or exceptions, and the secondary fallback absorbed enough traffic to appear as partial degradation rather than total primary failure.

Test suite gaps allowed the escape: differ-level dedup tests seed their own mock binding stores, apply-level tests seed synthetic id-bearing payloads, and no test crosses the seam between real transport (which carries no id field) and the recording/diffing layers.

Review criteria E4, T3, and T5b abstain or stop short at the exact boundary where the vulnerability lies: E4 explicitly abstains on external-system response-shape claims, T3 measures only endpoint existence (not response schema), and T5b is advisory on plan-level reliability.

Production observability never flagged the invariant violation: comment_ids held 0 entries while bindings grew to 2475 and outbound posts succeeded, remaining undetected in committed state across the feature's entire active window.

Silent fail-open guards on correctness-critical paths merit both code-review detection (now post-escape via 4c57247ff88) and operation-linked invariant monitoring (not yet implemented) to prevent recurrence.
